I will keep my land mainly in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the backbone of my farm and the crop pattern I know best after 40 years. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on that to protect yield in dry spells, but I will still keep my input use moderate because I farm 16.9 mu with family labor and I do not want to stretch myself too thin. I will put most of the land into wheat followed by maize on the same fields, and I will keep smaller areas in chili and cotton for cash income and to spread risk. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and uniformity, especially in maize, wheat, and chili. I will not chase the highest possible input level. I will use enough fertilizer to secure a steady crop, irrigate when the crop most needs water, and spray only as many times as I expect are needed in a normal year. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it matches my scale and is easier for me to manage.
